picks.why: colored bird’s-eye view of the walled town; only 1046 px wide, but #2 (same plate, BnF) would need a trim to 40% of its width

picks.what: View of the town, engraving from Merian’s Topographia Galliae
picks.why: true profile view with the cathedral towers and the citadel; volume published 1655–61

picks.what: View from the Croix du Capitaine, southwest of the town, watercolor
picks.why: color view with the Peyrou water tower and the old town; inscribed as sketched 14 November 1821, retouched January 1845

picks.what: General view over the rooftops, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: only general view of the period; color; frame and caption cut

picks.what: Saint-Pierre Cathedral above the old town, seen from the Corum, photograph
picks.why: recent, sharp view of the cathedral and the old town roofs

gaps: P0: nothing. P5: only a hazy 1928 aerial.
notes: P1 alternatives: #2 same Braun and Hogenberg plate in color at high resolution (BnF 1645 sheet; Montpellier is the top-left of three views), #5/#6 uncolored single sheets. P3 alternatives: #12 Laurens lithograph 1835 and #14 Laurens 1841 (black and white, town small in the distance). P4 alternative: #22 the Peyrou promenade with the Louis XIV statue and water tower (famous landmark scene). Skipped #23 Mittelholzer 1928 aerial: smoke and cloud cover most of the town.
